why: The statement is universal and unrestricted in dimension, so a single pair of homotopy-equivalent, non-homeomorphic closed aspherical 4-manifolds with the same fundamental group falsifies it as worded: the OpenAI manuscript is scored whole/refuted/counterexample, unreviewed (no human reader in 8 days, no Lean), and doubtful rather than not_credible because the doubts are specific (unreviewed MT/PD dependencies, the F2 non-goodness claim on an open question, unaddressed Khan tension) but no error is identified and the mechanism (non-good hyperbolic group, where 4-d rigidity is not known) is coherent. AI role is generated: author is 'OpenAI', no human is named, and the release README attributes the results to an internal model; this is release-level, not manuscript-level, but nothing suggests a human produced it. The companion MT/PD/boundary manuscripts answer different questions (disk embedding, goodness, Wall realisation) and are variants. Davis et al. refutes only the smooth analogue (variant); Davis-Hillman concern manifolds with boundary (variant); Khan is up to s-cobordism and GTY is stable (variants); Krushkal (goodness) and Aria (sorry-ended statement) are none. Class results (Farrell-Jones, Hsiang-Wall, Bartels-Lueck, FLS, Barcenas et al., Wang, Gkeneralis) are cases; Roushon is withdrawn.
doubts: openai-2026-borel-dim4 and openai-math-320 are the same manuscript recorded twice (research pass and OpenAI stage); I gave them identical answers. The AI attribution rests on a release-level README sentence that does not name this manuscript. Gkeneralis's result may be a direct instance of Bartels-Lueck (2012) and so not new. Whether a counterexample in dimension four alone counts as 'whole' depends on reading the bullet as a universal claim over all dimensions; the statement's wording supports that reading, though the literature treats the conjecture dimension by dimension and dimensions 4 and 5+ have different status.
